idea-plugin.name: TabCue: Visual Terminal Tabs
idea-plugin.description:
Give every terminal tab its own colour, emoji, icon and text colour, so five open terminals stop looking like one terminal.

I kept losing track of which was which. npm run dev, a couple of Claude sessions, and an ssh into something I would rather not typo in. They all look identical, and the IDE numbers them "Local (2)", "Local (3)" and leaves you to remember the rest.

Right-click any Terminal tab and choose Tab Style. Everything is there.

What it does

  • Colours. Eight presets, or any colour at all from the IDE's own colour picker, with live preview as you drag. Painted as the tab background and as a small dot beside the name.
  • Emoji. Twelve common ones are a single click in the tab menu, and Custom… takes anything else, including the system emoji palette on macOS.
  • Icons. Ten of the IDE's own, for when an emoji is too much.
  • Text colour. White, black or custom. This is the cue that stays put while a tab is selected.
  • Rules. Style tabs automatically by title or working directory, first match wins. Paint anything matching ssh prod red so you always know which machine you are on.
  • Background tint. Optionally tint the terminal output area too, not just the tab, at a strength you choose.

It does something before you configure anything: each terminal is given its own colour, derived from the tab's name and directory so it is still that colour tomorrow. Rules, auto colours and tint strength all live in Settings ▸ Tools ▸ TabCue, and auto colours can be switched off there if you would rather choose every one yourself.

Good to know

  • The IDE throws away a tab's background colour while that tab is selected, and paints its hover colour over it on hover. The dot, the emoji and the text colour are the cues that survive in every state, which is why the dot is on by default.
  • Split terminals share one colour, because a split is several sessions inside a single tab.
  • An AI agent tab the IDE has already marked with a vendor logo keeps it. The colour still applies, and an emoji you pick yourself still replaces the logo.
  • Works with both the reworked and the classic terminal engine, in any IntelliJ-based IDE that bundles the Terminal.
  • Rules live in .idea/terminalTabStyle.xml so you can commit and share them. Per-tab styles go in workspace.xml, because their keys contain local paths. Nothing leaves your machine.
